title: Stream Gatekeeper: preemptive quota rebalancer for continuous streaming batches
creator: Aasha Patel
description:
Problem: Long-running streaming/continuous-batching requests frequently tie up GPU working sets and KV cache residency, causing hard-to-observe SLO regressions for short interactive requests from higher-priority tenants. Existing preemptors evict aggressively or stop intake entirely which either increases tail latency or causes unnecessary cold-KV churn.

Goal: Implement a gatekeeper-style preemption layer that performs lightweight, periodic quota rebalancing ("pulse") to preserve interactive SLOs while minimizing KV cold miss rate and avoiding jarring GPU memory thrashing. The gatekeeper should be configurable by SLO tier and support soft preemption (grace windows) for streaming slices, with visibility in console dashboards and safe rollout steps.

Constraints: Must work with continuous-batching runtime that supports partial interrupts and KV checkpointing. Must not require model-level changes. Latency SLOs vary by customer tier; design needs to be multi-tenant aware and pluggable into existing slot allocator.
acceptance_criteria: New Stream Gatekeeper component deployed behind a feature flag on runtime-1.21
For synthetic mixed workload (70% short interactive, 30% long streams) P95 latency for short requests improves by >= 20% vs baseline under identical load
KV cold miss rate increase <= 10% when gatekeeper is active (measured over 1 hour windows)
No production incidents caused by rollout; automatic rollback knob in Console within 5 minutes
Dashboards show per-tenant gated-time, preemption-pulses, and estimated KV-residency impact
design_decisions: Pulse cadence: adaptive every 250ms-2s based on instantaneous queue depth and observed KV pressure
Soft preemption: streaming slices receive a grace-window of 50-300ms to flush KV writes and checkpoint; if still running, they are paused and requeued to avoid hard eviction
Quota accounting: allocate ephemeral pulse-quota tokens per tenant derived from their SLO weight and historical token consumption; tokens decay over 60s
KV-aware selection: when deciding which stream to pause, prefer streams with low expected KV working set (estimated from recent token/kv-access histograms) to minimize cold misses
Memory safety: gatekeeper requests a conservative GPU memory headroom reservation; if headroom < threshold, switch to aggressive pulse mode (shorter cadence, lower grace)
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Prototype (2w): implement gatekeeper logic in local runtime dev branch; simulate mixed workloads using bench-suite; produce microbench report
Phase 2 - Integration (3w): wire gatekeeper into slot allocator and KV residency tracker; emit metrics: gate.pulses, gate.pauses, gate.resume_latency, gate.kv_estimated_evictions
Phase 3 - Canary (2w): enable feature flag for internal tenant and one low-risk customer; run 48h canary and validate regressions
Phase 4 - Rollout (2w): staged rollout by region and tenant tier; enable console feature to dynamically tune cadence and grace windows
Phase 5 - Postmortem and iterate: collect telemetry for 30 days and iterate on selection heuristics
rollout_and_monitoring: Canary policy: start with non-production fleet -> 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% per-region escalation
SLO monitors: short-request P95 and P99, KV cold miss rate, GPU memory headroom, preemption-induced restarts
Alerting: page on short-request P99 increase > 15% for 5 minutes or gate.resume_latency > 500ms sustained
notes: 2025-11-05 - Kickoff: scoped requirement with PM (Jin Morales). Decided pulse approach after whiteboard session comparing continuous vs epochal preemption.

2025-11-12 - Prototype complete: bench-suite run shows short-request p95 improved by 18% with a static 500ms pulse; KV cold miss increased by 6%. Baseline attached: https://storage.redwood.ai/bench/ENG-632580/proto-report.pdf

2025-11-20 - Design review: feedback from runtime/kv team: make KV-access estimator conservative and add opt-out for latency-sensitive models. Action: add model opt-out label and per-tenant override. (Design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/879)
2025-11-28 - PR opened for gatekeeper core logic; initial tests flaky when GPU fragmentation high. Investigating memory headroom calculation; added simulated fragmentation tests.
2025-12-03 - Observability added: gate.pulses and gate.kv_eviction_estimated counters are emitted. Console card prototype ready for internal QA.

2025-12-08 - Canary started on internal-only fleet (region-us-east-1). Early telemetry: short P95 improved by 22% during busy window, resume_latency median 120ms, predicted KV evictions within tolerance

2025-12-10 - Blocker flagged: one internal tenant observed higher than expected resume_latency during GPU swap events. Tentative mitigation: increase grace-window adaptively when swap-rate > 2/min. Assigned to Marcus Liu for hotfix.
